docs.text: Yes, mostly Facebook is horrible, but I’m currently watching a bunch of Americans argue back and forth over whether states which contain/border the Great Lakes count as landlocked and it’s *fascinating*

i asked my wife to pull up her maps app and look at the great lakes/eastern seaboard. “in your opinion, are the great lakes states and pennsylvania landlocked? it’s a bluesky debate.” her first response: “how many fucking neurodivergent people are on that website?!?”

Putting Illinois as "Landlocked 2x" feels like it understates how much access Illinois has to the internal waterways that lead to the sea. We have the Great Lakes and the Mississippi river! We aren't really landlocked! We have multiple paths to the sea!

This makes sense now that I think about it, but in my defense I forgot about Lake Erie because I'm from the Pacific Northwest and I still think of the middle of the country as being landlocked. It was only four years ago that I realized the Great Lakes have *waves*.
Hard disagree. If the Great Lakes states aren’t landlocked then no state is. If you have to travel through another state to reach an ocean your state is landlocked.

having lived on both coasts, this take is clearly correct, but we must be clear-eyed and remember the real foe: landlocked states doubly so the weirdos who think the great lakes make them not landlocked
